text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright arrived in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo on Sunday to push for full compliance with the Dayton peace treaty, after reprimanding the presidents of Serbia and Croatia for failing to honour the agreement.

Albright was due to meet the Moslem, Croat and Serb members of the country's collective presidency as part of a U.S. effort to shore up the 1995 peace agreement, which ended four years of war in former Yugoslavia.
Albright was expected to warn Bosnian political leaders that the United States and European powers would impose penalites on any faction which violated provisions of the treaty.

She rebuked Bosnia's powerful neighbours on Saturday, demanding that Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic ensure the extradition of indicted war criminals and the safe return of refugees.
Albright was scheduled to fly by helicopter later on Sunday to the disputed northern town of Brcko to visit American troops serving in the NATO-led peace force.
